title: DEGAP: Dynamic Entropy-Guided Attention Perturbation
one_liner: A vision-language model hallucinates less by comparing its normal answer path to a perturbed version where visual attention is weakened at just the right depth.
lead: Large vision-language models (a model trained to understand both pictures and text) sometimes ignore what it sees and invent answers based purely on language patterns. DEGAP fixes this by making the model run two parallel forward passes: one normal, one where visual attention (the mechanism that focuses on image regions) is slightly disrupted. By comparing these two branches, the model learns when it should trust the picture over language habit.

paras: A large vision-language model learns two things: patterns in how humans use language (a language prior) and patterns in pictures (visual grounding). When it answers a question about an image, it can lean too heavily on the language prior.

A naive fix would be to ignore language and only look at the picture. But language patterns carry real signal—the model needs both. The real problem is telling when to trust the picture and when to trust the language. The model has no internal gauge of that choice.

callout.html: DEGAP forces the model to compare its normal answer path (both language and vision) against a contrast path where vision is artificially weakened, so the difference reveals when the model was relying on language habit instead of the picture.

panels.title: 1. Model sees both
panels.caption: Language patterns (left bars) and visual signals (right bars) both fire up in the model.

panels.title: 2. Hallucination path: language wins
panels.viz_args: Model: 'Apple brand logo' — but the image shows a red circle, not a logo.
panels.caption: Language prior dominates; model ignores the visual evidence against 'apple'.

panels.title: 3. Perturb visual attention
panels.caption: In the contrast branch, visual attention is weakened; language-only answer emerges.

panels.title: 4. Compare branches
panels.caption: The difference signals where language habit is steering the answer.

panels.title: 5. Correct decision: trust the picture
panels.caption: Visual signals gain weight; model learns to say 'red circle', not a brand.

steps.text: Run the model on the image and question with all visual attention active.
Run the same image and question but artificially weaken visual attention at selected depths.
At each layer, calculate entropy (uncertainty) of the model's intermediate scores.
Perturb layers where entropy is low (the model is confident but may be overconfident).
Subtract the perturbed logits (raw score for each word) from the normal logits; the difference steers the model away from pure language habit.

paras: DEGAP modifies the attention weights inside the model during decoding (the phase when the model writes out its answer). Specifically, it weakens the visual attention connections at certain layers while keeping language attention unchanged.

hidden.h2: Entropy: how confident is the model?
hidden.name: Confidence-weighted entropy
paras: Entropy is a number that measures how uncertain things are. If a model is very sure one word comes next, entropy is low. If all words seem equally likely, entropy is high. Here, entropy tells us whether the model is confidently picking one path or hedging across many possibilities.

DEGAP measures entropy at each layer and uses it to decide where to perturb. If entropy is already high (the model is uncertain), perturbation there will not help, because the model is already spreading its bets across many words—weakening visual attention won't change which word wins. If entropy is low (the model is overconfident), perturbation reveals whether that confidence is justified by the picture or by language habit, because a confident decision that drops sharply when vision is weakened was driven by language, not the image.

heat.caption: Darker means lower entropy, more confident. Highlighted layers are where DEGAP perturbs attention to test whether confidence is vision-grounded.

reads.html: The model is most confident (darkest) in the middle layers, where language patterns and visual signals meet. Perturbing there exposes over-reliance on language.

Layer-wise entropy measures the model's certainty at intermediate steps in the computation. DEGAP selects layers where entropy is below a threshold, indicating high confidence that deserves validation by contrastive perturbation.

mechanism.h2: Why weakening visual attention reveals hallucination
paras: A vision-language model fuses language and visual signals through attention. Attention is a mechanism (a soft gate) that decides which parts of the image to look at. When the model hallucinates, it has learned language patterns so well that those patterns pull the answer even when the visual evidence contradicts them.

DEGAP's core insight: run the model twice. In the contrast run, visual attention is weakened at layers where the model is overconfident. This forces the model to answer using only language habit. If the contrast answer is very different from the normal answer, the model was relying on language habit in the normal path. If both paths agree, the answer is grounded in the picture. By comparing, the model learns to discount answers that lean too far on language alone.

stages.s: Normal branch: all visual attention active
Measure entropy at each layer to find overconfident decisions
Contrast branch: visual attention weakened at selected layers
Final answer steered toward vision-grounded words

math.words: The next-word score is the normal branch score minus a scaled perturbed branch score. The scaling factor depends on the model's confidence at that layer.
symbols: log-probability of a word under normal forward pass
log-probability of a word when visual attention is weakened
weighting factor (higher = trust the perturbation more)
adjusted score that the model uses to pick the next word

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Scenario: model is choosing next word after 'The image shows a...'
Normal branch outputs score_normal for word 'circle' = 2.5 (likely)
Perturbed branch outputs score_perturbed for word 'circle' = 0.3 (unlikely when vision is weak)
This high contrast (2.5 - 0.3 = 2.2) signals the word 'circle' is vision-grounded.
Low contrast (2.0 - 1.9 = 0.1) signals 'logo' is driven by language habit, not vision.
With alpha = 1.0: score_final for 'circle' = 2.5 - 0.3 = 2.2; score_final for 'logo' = 2.0 - 1.9 = 0.1.
Model picks 'circle' over 'logo', the vision-grounded answer.

math.note: The difference between branches acts as a filter: words that both branches agree on are vision-grounded; words only the normal branch likes are language habit and get downweighted.

charts.title: Naive vision-language model
charts.note: The model hallucinates by making up details not in the image, usually because language patterns are too strong.

charts.title: With DEGAP contrastive decoding
charts.note: Comparing normal and perturbed branches filters out language-driven mistakes. Contrastive decoding steers answers toward the image.

items.html: If visual attention is barely weakened, the contrast branch still uses enough visual signal and the difference between branches vanishes. The model learns no corrective signal.
If visual attention is crushed to zero, the contrast branch may produce nonsense (random language), and the difference becomes so large it over-steers away from legitimate visual descriptions.
If the model perturbs layers that process language only, visual attention is unaffected and hallucination persists. Entropy guidance must correctly identify layers where language and vision interact.
Entropy-guided layer selection ensures perturbation hits layers where the model is overconfident about mixed signals. The difference between branches is stable and informative.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Write a short script that loads a vision-language model (e.g., a smaller CLIP-based model or a Qwen-VL setup) and an image where the model commonly hallucinates (e.g., confusing object color or mistaking an object category based on language bias). Run a forward pass with standard decoding to see the hallucination. Then implement DEGAP by calculating layer-wise entropy, selecting low-entropy layers, and running a perturbed forward pass where you scale down the visual attention weights by 50% at those layers. Compare the two branches and decode using the contrastive score. The demo should make it obvious that the perturbed branch outputs pure language habit, and the difference between branches steers the model toward the true visual content.
demo.metric_eq: hallucination_rate = (count of wrong answers) / (total answers); show that DEGAP reduces this vs. standard decoding
demo.closing: The demo must show side-by-side: (1) standard model answer (hallucination), (2) perturbed-only answer (language bias alone), (3) DEGAP contrastive answer (vision-grounded). The human eye should see the model escaping language habit by comparing the two branches.
